overview: Li Ning Company Limited is one of China's leading sports brand companies, designing, developing, manufacturing, marketing and distributing footwear, apparel, equipment and accessories under the core LI-NING brand across professional and leisure sports categories (running, basketball, training, badminton, table tennis and sports casual, plus emerging outdoor/tennis/pickleball segments). The Group also holds minority/JV interests in Double Happiness (table tennis), AIGLE (outdoor) and Kason (badminton). Operations are overwhelmingly China-domestic (over 98% of FY2025 revenue), distributed through a 7,609-POS network (FY2025) of franchised distributors, directly-operated retail, LI-NING YOUNG (kids) and e-commerce channels, with reporting currency RMB and an HKD-quoted, Cayman-incorporated listing structure.

business_model.summary: Li Ning designs and markets sportswear sold through a hybrid wholesale/retail/e-commerce network; franchised distributors are the largest and fastest-growing channel (46.6% of FY2025 revenue, +6.3% YoY), followed by e-commerce (29.5%, +5.3% YoY) and directly-operated retail (22.5%, down as the Group rationalises underperforming stores). Footwear and apparel are the two largest product categories (49.5% and 41.6% of FY2025 revenue respectively), with equipment/accessories a smaller but faster-growing category (+12.7% in FY2025). Revenue is largely transactional/seasonal (driven by new product launches and sell-through) rather than contractually recurring, though the extensive franchise network and growing membership-based direct retail provide some repeat-purchase stability.
business_model.customer_type: B2C (end consumers via owned/franchised retail and e-commerce) with a B2B wholesale layer to franchised distributors
business_model.geographic_mix: The PRC market ~98.6% of FY2025 revenue (Northern region 47.3%, Southern region 51.3% of PRC revenue); other regions (South Korea, Hong Kong, Macau, limited international) ~1.4%

main_competitors: Li Ning's own sub-brand overlap (China Li-Ning fashion line)
competitive_position.market_position: Third/fourth-largest sportswear brand in China by revenue, well behind Anta Sports (FY2025 revenue ~RMB80bn, roughly 2.7x Li Ning's ~RMB29.6bn) and behind or near Nike China/Adidas China; domestic Chinese brands collectively have grown from under 30% of the China sportswear market in 2015 to roughly 50% by 2025, with Li Ning positioned as a mid-premium professional-sports specialist rather than the scale leader

moat_factors.description: Founded by Olympic gymnast Li Ning; official partner of the Chinese Olympic Committee, supplying award uniforms for major Games (2026 Milan Winter Olympics, 2025 World Games), which reinforces a patriotic, professional-sports brand identity that is hard for competitors (including foreign brands) to replicate in China

Proprietary cushioning technologies (Super BOOM, Super BOOM Capsule, BOOM Fiber, GCU outsole system) support premiumization and professional credibility, evidenced by strong share in competitive running shoe segments (e.g., 61.35% share among elite finishers under 90 minutes at the Beijing Half Marathon)

7,609 POS as of FY2025 across franchised, direct and LI-NING YOUNG formats provide broad distribution reach, though the network is static/slow-growing (+0.3% POS YoY) rather than a source of expansion-driven growth
Materially smaller than Anta Sports, limiting purchasing scale, marketing budget and ability to match multi-brand portfolio diversification (Anta also owns Fila, Descente, Kolon in China)

weaknesses: Single-brand concentration (LI-NING core brand) versus Anta's multi-brand portfolio approach, limiting diversification across price points and consumer segments
Declining direct-retail channel and compressed gross margin from channel mix shift and heavier discounting/promotional competition
Minimal international diversification (~1.4% of revenue), leaving the business almost entirely exposed to the Chinese consumer cycle
Historical brand/value perception gap versus Anta and international brands in some premium segments; China Li-Ning fashion sub-line had cooled from its earlier 'China-chic' hype cycle

growth_drivers: Technology-driven product upgrades (Super BOOM Capsule midsole, aerospace-derived thermal/cooling technologies) supporting premiumization and share gains in running, basketball and table tennis

Deepened Chinese Olympic Committee partnership through the Olympic cycle (2026 Milan Winter Olympics, future Games), including the new premium 'Glory Gold Label' product series co-branded with the COC emblem
Expansion into emerging/niche categories - outdoor (COUNTERFLOW concept store), tennis and pickleball - as traditional category growth plateaus
New retail store-format innovation (LOONG Store flagship, standalone outdoor stores, Forbidden City-themed specialty zones) to re-accelerate same-store productivity
Continued e-commerce and new/emerging e-commerce platform (e.g., Xiaohongshu, Douyin) monetization

New global athlete/IP partnerships (e.g., long-term strategic cooperation with NBA star Stephen Curry's Curry Brand announced in H1 2026) to extend international visibility and basketball category credibility
Supply chain/manufacturing investment (Guangxi high-end intelligent manufacturing and R&D base, ~RMB3.3bn planned investment) to improve flexibility and cost structure
Policy tailwinds: China's 15th Five-Year Plan and national sports-industry policy targeting a sports-industry scale of over RMB7 trillion by 2030

business.risk: Intensifying competition from Anta Sports and international brands (Nike, Adidas) regaining share in China
business.description: Anta is roughly 2.7x Li Ning's revenue scale and operates a multi-brand portfolio; Nike/Adidas China have shown signs of stabilizing/recovering share, compressing the window for domestic challengers

Gross margin declined as channel mix shifted toward lower-margin franchised distribution and promotional discounting intensified in self-operated channels (FY2025 gross margin 49.0%, down 0.4pp YoY); inventory turnover remains elevated at ~64-65 days
Directly-operated retail revenue fell 3.3% in FY2025 and POS count fell 4.5% YoY as the Group closes underperforming stores, indicating offline productivity pressure
Unlike Anta's multi-brand strategy, Li Ning relies almost entirely on the core LI-NING brand (plus minority JV stakes in Double Happiness/AIGLE/Kason), concentrating fashion/demand risk

Ongoing Hong Kong High Court litigation (Active Legend/Vast Gold writ of summons) alleging a HK$500m+ loan obligation at a subsidiary acquired in 2021 (Li Ning Communications HK, formerly Matsunichi); management believes no repayment obligation exists but the matter is unresolved as of H1 2026

financial.description: FY2025 effective tax rate rose to 29.9% from 26.7% due to withholding tax on cross-border capital structure planning, pressuring net margins despite stable operating profit

The Group does not hedge FX; holds cash/pays dividends, license fees and certain investments in HKD, USD, EUR, KRW and GBP against an RMB reporting base and functional-currency subsidiaries in Korea/HK/Macau
H1 2026 operating cash flow fell sharply to RMB954m from RMB2,411m in H1 2025, reflecting higher cash-based marketing/tax outlays and e-commerce platform settlement timing lags
FY2025 included a full RMB72.4m goodwill impairment (2009 Kason Sports acquisition) and RMB269m of investment property impairment reflecting weak Chinese mainland/Hong Kong property markets

regulatory.description: Business benefits from government domestic-demand stimulus policies; any reversal or ineffectiveness of stimulus could remove a tailwind

regulatory.risk: Cayman Islands incorporation / Hong Kong listing structure
regulatory.description: Standard offshore-listing governance and potential cross-border regulatory considerations typical of PRC-operating, HK-listed issuers

macro.description: Management explicitly cited 'structural divergence in the consumer market' and 'strong supply and weak demand' contradictions in H1 2026; sportswear is a discretionary category highly exposed to Chinese consumer confidence, income growth and the property-market-linked wealth effect
Intensified discounting across self-operated and e-commerce channels industry-wide is compressing sector gross margins
The Group holds investment properties (including a Hong Kong office/retail property acquired in 2024) exposed to soft Hong Kong/mainland property price and rental trends, driving impairments

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China sportswear retail sales showed renewed momentum entering 2026 (Jefferies flagged >5% growth for Jan-Feb 2026 after a flat Q4 2025), helped by Lunar New Year demand, Winter Olympics visibility and domestic-demand stimulus policy; longer-term, China's national sports-industry policy targets an industry scale exceeding RMB7 trillion by 2030, and domestic brands' combined China market share has risen from under 30% (2015) to roughly 50% (2025), though growth across the sector has decelerated from historical double-digit rates to low-single/mid-single-digit rates for the larger players
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high - sportswear is consumer discretionary and sensitive to the Chinese economic cycle, consumer confidence and property-market wealth effects, though the 'sports participation'/health secular trend provides some structural support distinct from pure fashion cyclicality
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (net cash position, no outstanding borrowings against RMB14.1bn credit facilities as of H1 2026); indirect sensitivity via Chinese consumer credit conditions and property-market linked wealth effects
key_input_costs: Labor costs at manufacturing/supply chain partners
Marketing and athlete/IP sponsorship costs (COC partnership, Stephen Curry deal)

recent_developments.event: Analyst sentiment mixed-to-positive: consensus ~25 Buy/4 Hold/1 Sell across ~29 analysts with average 12-month target around HK$22-26 (JPMorgan Overweight HK$23-25.6, Goldman Sachs Buy HK$22.80, Macquarie Buy HK$21.30, Citi Buy HK$22.80) versus Nomura Hold HK$16.00 and a prior Bernstein/SocGen Sell at HK$18.00, reflecting debate over the pace of China sportswear demand recovery

H1 2026 interim results released: revenue up 2.8% YoY to RMB15,235m, gross margin improved to 50.9% (from 50.0%), profit attributable to equity holders up 4.5% YoY to RMB1,816m, but operating cash flow fell sharply to RMB954m (from RMB2,411m in H1 2025); interim dividend raised to RMB35.12 cents/share (from RMB33.59 cents)

Entered a long-term strategic partnership with NBA superstar Stephen Curry and his 'Curry Brand' covering basketball equipment R&D, event marketing and new-generation consumer engagement - a notable step toward international brand visibility

Launched the premium 'LI-NING Glory Gold Label' product series (first to jointly use the Chinese Olympic Committee emblem and LI-NING logo) and opened pop-up 'Loong Store' formats tied to Winter Olympics marketing, with a flagship Loong Store planned for H2 2026
Supplied award uniforms/equipment for the Chinese Sports Delegation at the 2026 Milan Winter Olympics and the 2026 Asian Beach Games (Sanya), reinforcing the Olympic-partner brand positioning

Opened the world's first LI-NING 'Loong Store' in Beijing alongside the Glory Gold Label launch, and opened the first standalone outdoor concept store 'COUNTERFLOW' as part of category diversification into outdoor sports

FY2025 full-year results: revenue up 3.2% to RMB29,598m, gross margin declined slightly to 49.0% (from 49.4%) on channel mix shift and promotional intensity, profit attributable to equity holders declined 2.6% to RMB2,936m on a higher effective tax rate (29.9% vs 26.7%); POS count roughly flat at 7,609 (+0.3%)

Ongoing Hong Kong High Court litigation: a 2025 statutory demand (subsequently withdrawn) and 2025-26 writ of summons from liquidators of Active Legend/Vast Gold alleging a HK$500m+ legacy loan obligation at a subsidiary (Li Ning Communications HK) acquired in 2021; case management conference scheduled for September 2026, with management maintaining there is no repayment obligation

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Results (20 August 2026) / FY2025 Annual Report Outlook

items.target: No specific numerical guidance disclosed; qualitative 'steady growth' expectation
items.notes: Management has not issued formal quantitative revenue guidance in recent filings; FY2025 outlook language emphasized 'steady performance growth' and 'high-quality development' rather than specific targets, consistent with H1 2026 commentary describing a 'fluctuating retail environment'

items.target: ~50% of profit attributable to equity holders
items.notes: FY2025 total dividend of RMB56.95 cents/share represented a 50% payout ratio; H1 2026 interim dividend of RMB35.12 cents was raised from RMB33.59 cents in H1 2025, consistent with continuation of the payout policy

items.metric: Capital investment - Guangxi supply chain base
items.target: Up to approximately RMB3.3 billion total investment
items.notes: As of H1 2026, carrying value of non-current assets under this investment was RMB2,122m (~5.5% of total assets); funded by unutilised top-up placing proceeds and internal resources

items.target: Four pillars: (1) technology-driven product upgrades, (2) Olympic marketing/brand building via COC partnership, (3) dual improvement in operational quality and efficiency (channel optimization, inventory turnover acceleration), (4) strengthening talent/finance/digital foundations
items.notes: Articulated in the FY2025 annual report Outlook section as qualitative strategic priorities rather than numerical targets

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Li Ning's FY2025 statement emphasized 'steady growth' amid a 'stable' but uncertain China macro environment, highlighting the Olympic partnership and technology commercialization (Super BOOM Capsule) as key value drivers for 2026. The H1 2026 MD&A struck a more cautious tone, citing 'severe challenges of a complex and volatile external trade landscape' and 'pronounced domestic contradictions of strong supply and weak demand,' while noting the Group is prioritizing 'healthy inventory levels' and 'operating quality' over aggressive growth targets in a 'fluctuating retail environment.'

bull_case: Net-cash balance sheet (no outstanding borrowings against RMB14.1bn in credit facilities) with a ~50% dividend payout ratio provides capital-return support and balance sheet resilience through a soft consumer cycle

Deepening Chinese Olympic Committee partnership and new international athlete tie-ups (Stephen Curry/Curry Brand) support premiumization (Glory Gold Label) and brand differentiation versus both domestic and international competitors

Proprietary cushioning technology (Super BOOM Capsule) is gaining genuine competitive traction in professional running, evidenced by rising category market share and strong marathon elite-runner penetration
Diversification into emerging categories (outdoor, tennis, pickleball) and new store formats (Loong Store, COUNTERFLOW) offers incremental growth vectors beyond a maturing core category base

Analyst consensus skews Buy (roughly 25 of 29 covering analysts) with price targets implying meaningful upside from current levels, reflecting expectations of a China sportswear demand inflection in 2026
bear_case: Scale disadvantage versus Anta Sports (roughly 2.7x Li Ning's revenue) and a single-brand strategy leave Li Ning structurally exposed to share loss as Anta's multi-brand portfolio and Nike/Adidas China's recovery squeeze the middle of the market

Management's own H1 2026 commentary flags 'weak demand' and a 'fluctuating retail environment,' with revenue growth decelerating to low single digits and operating cash flow falling sharply (RMB954m vs RMB2,411m in H1 2025)
Gross margin and channel economics are under structural pressure from a mix shift toward lower-margin wholesale/franchise channels and intensifying promotional discounting

Almost total reliance on the Chinese consumer (~98.6% of revenue) with negligible international diversification leaves the business fully exposed to China's uneven consumption recovery and property-market-linked wealth effects

Unresolved legacy litigation (Active Legend/Vast Gold HK$500m+ claim) and recent goodwill/investment-property impairments add episodic uncertainty, even if currently viewed as low-probability financial risks
